items.stem: Explain why the area of a triangle is half the area of a rectangle with the same base and height.
items.answer: Drawing the diagonal of the rectangle splits it into two identical triangles, each with that base and height.
items.markingKey: B1 two congruent triangles; B1 so half [2]

items.stem: Explain why the slanted side of a parallelogram is not used to calculate its area.
items.answer: Area needs the perpendicular height; the slanted side is longer than the height, so using it would overestimate the area.
items.markingKey: B1 perpendicular height needed; B1 slant longer [2]

items.stem: A cone has radius 5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. Lucas uses πrl with l = 12 to get the curved surface area 188 cm². Explain the mistake and find the correct curved surface area.

items.stem: Explain why a cylinder can be treated as a prism when finding its volume.
items.answer: It has the same circular cross-section all the way along its length, so V = πr² × h.

items.stem: Explain why doubling the radius of a cylinder (keeping the height) multiplies the volume by 4, but doubling the height only doubles it.
items.answer: V = πr²h: r is squared, so ×2 in r gives ×4; h is to the power 1, so ×2 in h gives ×2.
